items.title: The Best Games Like GTA 6 to Play on PC in 2026
items.summary: Looking for open-world chaos without the wait? From Cyberpunk 2077 to indie gems like Shakedown: Hawaii, here are the best games like GTA 6.
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is set to be a titanic shift in gaming for a lot of people. However, it’s also going to cost a fair bit of cash, and its specific vibe might not be for everyone. Exploring a massive open world is a lot of fun, and GTA 6 certainly doesn’t have a monopoly on how you can go about it. Whether you’re looking to tide yourself over until you can justify the expense, or you simply want an open-world crime game with a different flavour, we’re going to help you out with the best games like GTA 6.

While there’s one very obvious answer on the list here, we’ve tried to keep things varied. There are plenty of fantastic open-world sandboxes available right now, and we can always spice things up with a few genre shifts and indie gems. Let’s get into the list.

Cyberpunk 2077 is a wildly different game from the one it was at launch. Night City is now a seamless open world filled with an absurd number of characters to talk to, weapons to master, and ways to approach every mission. With overhauled vehicle combat, fancier cyberware augments, and a world that’s eye-wateringly beautiful to explore, we’d argue that this is one of the best open-world RPGs ever made.

Saints Row IV is easily the silliest entry in the series. It puts you in the shoes of the President of the United States right as aliens invade Earth and trap humanity inside a virtual simulation. The bad news is, well, all of that. The good news is that being in a simulation means you get to unlock superpowers—some of which allow you to create tornadoes just by sprinting down the street. It’s also fully co-op, meaning you and a friend can enjoy the open-world chaos together.

This is the obvious pick if you haven’t played it yet and want a game that’s almost exactly like GTA 6 without actually being GTA 6. It lets you play as three distinct protagonists whose lives constantly intersect throughout a story packed with ups, downs, and plenty of anger. Alongside an incredible single-player sandbox in Los Santos, it also grants you access to GTA Online, which remains an unmatched multiplayer experience.

Watch_Dogs 2 is an absolute delight of an open-world adventure. You play as a hacker named Marcus, who uses a weaponised thunderball (basically a heavy-duty yo-yo) to knock people out and has a bone to pick with a corrupt tech CEO. Thankfully, you’re not alone; you’ll team up with the hacker collective DedSec to take down the system. It’s a vibrant, upbeat experience that lets you hack nearly anything in San Francisco in an instant, and it still looks stunning today.

If you’ve ever wanted to play GTA set in Hong Kong, then Sleeping Dogs is the game for you. It places a much heavier focus on martial arts combat than GTA does, delivering a constant string of cinematic set pieces as you try to take down a massive Triad organisation from within as an undercover cop. This is a tense, brutal crime drama set in a gorgeous world filled with plenty of distractions alongside hard-hitting story moments.

We’re moving into the indie section of this list now, so please enjoy. Tiny Terry’s Turbo Trip is an absurdist, charming take on the open-world city game. Your main goal is to launch yourself into space in your car, and you’ll do whatever it takes to accomplish that. You can run around committing petty crimes, stealing turbo junk, crashing into townsfolk, and gliding around town while being a general menace.

Retro City Rampage DX is, in essence, an 8-bit demake of a classic GTA game packed with homages to countless retro titles and pop culture icons. This leans much closer to an unhinged arcade game, really, but it’s an absolute blast to play. If you want the chaotic vibes of GTA in bite-sized chunks—complete with cardboard boxes to hide in and high-speed police chases—you’ll adore this.

From the creators of Retro City Rampage, Shakedown: Hawaii is all about building a “very reasonable” corporate empire in a 16-bit open world. You’re just looking to make some money, and sometimes that means shaking down local shops, extorting businesses, or resorting to over-the-top violence—all in the name of legitimate enterprise. It feels like a classic top-down GTA game lost in time, and it’s endlessly entertaining in how bombastic it is.

Jason likes to focus on roguelikes and co-op games; in a dream world he'd make a living writing about Dark Souls. As well as being a writer he also does personal training and accounting and can occasionally be seen on other people's streams. Being a big fan of fluffy things means he has two cats, both of whom refuse to let him sleep, but at least they are cute.

items.title: Can We Have A Good 'Blade Runner' Game In A Post-Cyberpunk World?
items.summary: Can the genre titan make an impact after CD Projekt Red borrowed so much from it?
items.content:
Can the genre titan make an impact after CD Projekt Red borrowed so much from it?

Amazon Prime Video While there are precursor examples that laid the groundwork for what it would become, it was the 1980s when cyberpunk crystallized as a sci-fi subgenre. Crucial works like Bruce Bethke’s “Cyberpunk ,” William Gibson’s Neuromancer , and Katsuhiro Otomo’s Akira came out of that era, pushing the movement into the mainstream and paving the way for the look and feel we all recognize now. Without those suffocating megacities and neon-lit dystopias, we wouldn’t have work like The Matrix or Altered Carbon.

One of the most consequential cyberpunk works came out the same year that Bethke coined the term: Blade Runner, Ridley Scott’s endlessly iconic adaptation of Phillip K. Dick’s Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? Initially met with lukewarm critical reception, the passage of time and the 1992 release of the Director’s Cut made it one of the most critically acclaimed pieces of cinematic sci-fi ever released, one so well-regarded that it received a 2017 sequel and a television follow-up set to debut later this month. Now, there are rumblings about a potential Blade Runner game on the horizon, although that raises the question of how effective one would be in a medium already suffused with its influence.

Blade Runner is critical to the foundation of cyberpunk.

In a recent interview with IGN , co-CEO of Alcon Entertainment (which owns the rights to the Blade Runner franchise) Andrew Kosove was asked whether the company had entertained the thought of a AAA Blade Runner game, to which he said “yes.” He went on to specify that the ability to “interact” with the franchise’s world was paramount, which makes sense because Blade Runner introduced a fascinating, lived-in setting filled with intriguing worldbuilding and eccentric characters. Kosove made these statements while promoting the upcoming Amazon streaming series Blade Runner 2099, another example of the franchise trying to expand that world beyond what was glimpsed in the 1982 original.

Blade Runner isn’t totally unfamiliar to the world of video games: there was a very loose Commodore 64 adaptation published in 1985, a beloved point-and-click adventure released for PC in 1997 (and re-released in 2022), and a VR tie-in that dropped in 2017 to coincide with the release of Blade Runner 2049. But it’s hard to claim that the IP has truly taken advantage of the format, especially since video game technology has surged forward. The last time the series had an original, full-scale video game outing was the same year that Titanic was released, which is a shame, because it’s a franchise perfectly suited for something like a 2010s Telltale treatment.

Despite being well-remembered enough to get a remaster, the 1997 point-and-click adventure was the last serious attempt at a Blade Runner game.

The other big problem the Blade Runner IP faces today is its own outsized cultural presence. While it’s obviously been a huge inspiration on work like the Deus Ex series, Blade Runner’s clearest descendant is Cyberpunk 2077, the hit 2020 action RPG. Ironically, both were plagued by issues upon release, then experienced a revision that led to significant critical acclaim.

Cyberpunk and the tabletop game it’s based on borrow many cues from the original film, from a dystopian American city ravaged by the excesses of an unethical corporatocracy to its everlasting questions about humanity and new forms of consciousness. While Blade Runner obviously came first, should Alcon and any potential developers be concerned about a potential video game being held to 2077’s high standard?

The world of Cyberpunk 2077 is a heightened take on Ridley Scott’s decidedly dour film.

Blade Runner does differ from Cyberpunk in some key ways; its world of authoritarian bounty hunters and humanistic liberationist androids is very different from CD Projekt Red’s vision of a future consumed by cybernetic modification and navigated by skillful hackers. There are a lot of directions you could take a premise as varied as Blade Runner ; it could be an action-heavy RPG building on the Cyberpunk 2077 formula, or it could be a narrative-centric interactive movie in the vein of something like Detroit: Become Human. But whatever form a game takes, it will have to do something to stand out from the very crowd it helped create.

10 Open-World Games Better Than Elden Ring in 2026
items.summary: Elden Ring is a fantastic game, but open-world games like The Witcher 3 are even better.
items.content:
Image via FromSoftware Add CBR on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By George Chrysostomou Published Nov 16, 2026, 10:30 PM EST George is an experienced entertainment and creative writer and a politics fan. If he's not talking about the latest MCU release, he's probably focused on local by-elections. With a love for analyzing detailed character work and a penchant for speculating on the upcoming twists and turns of major franchises, George is ultimately fascinated by the creative process. Sign in to your CBR account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread 6 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Elden Ring quickly became one of the most popular open-world games of all time when it was released in 2022. Four years later, in 2026, many gamers still consider it to be the best game in the genre, but there are a few open-world games, like Ghost of Yōtei , that arguably surpass it.

There's no denying that Elden Ring is an incredible game, but it's not for everyone due to its challenging combat and a story that's told more through lore than a traditional narrative. Open-world games like The Witcher 3 have stronger narratives, and other games give players more freedom, which is why they're the best games in the genre today.

Red Dead REdemption 2 screenshot showing Arthur on a horse riding through a mostly empty Western town Image via Rockstar Red Dead Redemption 2 gets plenty of attention, but its reputation is well earned. Once players get through its slower opening, they're free to explore a sprawling Wild West inspired by real history and locations. Rockstar fills that world with small details and dynamic encounters, designed to make it feel unusually alive.

Like Elden Ring , Red Dead Redemption 2 rewards players who wander off the beaten path, with countless hidden secrets and unexpected encounters waiting to be discovered. Where RDR2 has the advantage is in its commitment to realism. Combined with its accessible gunplay, those systems create a level of immersion that few open-world games can match.

Image via Sucker Punch Ghost of Tsushima was already one of the strongest open-world games of its generation, and Ghost of Yōtei builds on nearly everything that made it work. The sequel expands the formula with a more flexible approach to exploration and combat, creating another immersive experience that rarely forces players down a single path.

Where Ghost of Yōtei really pulls ahead of Elden Ring is in its character-driven storytelling. Atsu's journey gives the adventure a more personal emotional core. It also offers surprisingly precise combat, which makes switching between weapons feel fast and satisfying.It's remarkably easy to get lost in Ghost of Yōtei 's world.

Image via CD Projekt Red The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and Elden Ring are often compared, and for good reason. Both rank among the best fantasy open-world games ever made , with memorable bosses and plenty of freedom to explore. Where The Witcher 3 has the clear advantage, though, is in its storytelling.

Open-world games like Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 are the best games of their kind.

Geralt may look like a typical gruff fantasy anti-hero, but The Witcher 3 gives him, Ciri, Yennefer, and the rest of the game's supporting cast far more emotional depth than players might expect. Its strongest moments work because the relationships feel personal. Elden Ring excels at environmental storytelling, but The Witcher 3 delivers a more character-driven experience.

Image via Insomniac Games The first Spider-Man game from Insomniac Games was a stunning reimagining of the superhero world and a testament to Marvel's most popular character. The Miles Morales spinoff was equally exceptional, adding further depth to Miles Morales. Spider-Man 2 is the perfect follow-up, and while it might be underrated by fans, it's a more complete experience than Elden Ring .

Much could be said about the way the game tackles Peter's personal relationships and the famous Venom arc. Even more could be discussed surrounding the improved web-slinging mechanics and the flow of combat. What really deserves praise, however, is the seamless way this open-world title portrays a duo of leading heroes, giving ample time and energy to each.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Multiplayer Finally Goes Live
items.content:
Cyberpunk 2077 game cover Add ScreenRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Tom Wilson Published Nov 16, 2026, 6:32 AM EST Tom Wilson is a Gaming Features Writer at Screen Rant. Over the past five years, Tom has worked as the Editor-in-Chief at The Game Crater, as a Staff Writer for GamingIntel, a List Writer at TheGamer, and, of course, as a Senior Writer at ScreenRant. Tom has experience writing reviews, guides, news, and features, and has been responsible for teams of writers, training them and editing their work. Tom graduated with a Masters in Multimedia Journalism, and has since gone on to build up his portfolio of games journalism work. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Cyberpunk 2077 is the game that keeps on growing. CD Projekt Red, six years after the base game dropped, has released numerous updates of varying significance, as well as the critically acclaimed expansion and assorted expanded media releases. There is simply no shortage of ways to interact with Night City and the wider Cyberpunk world, unless you want to do so with a friend, of course. Cyberpunk 2077's official multiplayer was canceled back in 2021, with CD Projekt Red stating there are no plans to implement it in the future.

Naturally, this proved to be a huge blow to the game's fanbase, who had dreamed of roaming through Night City with their friends. However, it also proved to be a challenge for modders, who have since set about implementing what CD Projekt Red lacked the resources and time for. We've gotten announcements of a Far Cry -esque Cyberpunk 2077 co-op mod that makes the entire game's story playable with a friend, as well as a full-blown multiplayer experience which has finally gone live.

CyberMP is a mod that has been in the works for years. Its goal has always been to bring multiplayer to the streets of Night City and give players complete freedom over what that looks like. Offering the ability to create one's own server, CyberMP gives hosts control over almost every element of their version of Night City, including NPCs, world events, rules, economy, and more. It's impressive and has the potential to lead to complete reinventions of the core gameplay loop of Cyberpunk 2077 , much in the same way GTA Online does for GTA V .

CyberMP currently allows players to engage in PvP warfare, street races, and roleplaying, all of which are synchronized perfectly across each user's copy of the game. So, cars, unique player outfits, and every action will be seen simultaneously. This is made possible through fast network code as well as Easy Anti-Cheat, which prevents malicious actors from disrupting the server and ruining everyone's experience.

There are plans to add additional features and functions to CyberMP over the coming months, including proximity chat, which would allow for a greater degree of roleplaying potential. Currently, you can download the client from the mod's official website to join existing servers or host your own. It is in its Beta form, so prospective players should expect a myriad of bugs and missing features. However, for the most part, this is the intended CyberMP experience, offering a suite of impressive multiplayer features within Cyberpunk 2077 for the very first time.

It is worth noting that CyberMP is only available for the PC version of Cyberpunk 2077 .

Additionally, CyberMP has been designed with modders in mind, ensuring that the project can be expanded upon by anyone, thus making the possibilities for new features ostensibly endless. It's an exciting addition to the pantheon of amazing Cyberpunk 2077 mods , and a must-have for anyone who's been eagerly anticipating the day that the game finally gets its long-overdue multiplayer offering. Considering just how expansive Cyberpunk 2077's roleplaying options were before CyberMP's launch, fans are undoubtedly in for a world of new and exciting possibilities.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 PC players can finally become Night City heroes in original expansion mod
items.summary: Make a difference in Night City 🚑
items.content:
This Cyberpunk 2077 PC mod lets you join one of Night City's most-famous emergency response teams.

In another lifetime, Cyberpunk 2077 could have been the biggest release of the decade, even surpassing Grand Theft Auto VI , had it launched in the intended way.

Over the years though, it’s become the game it was always meant to be, and official mod support on PC, PlayStation and Xbox platforms make it even better.

If you want to make a real difference in Night City, drop the cyberware upgrades, forget the bounty hunting, and join the Trauma Team through this awesome in-progress expansion mod.

Going a step beyond what you’d typically expect of a questline mod, Join Trauma Team - AV Rescue Shifts introduces a fully-voiced team of characters who you’ll join on dangerous retrieval missions.

You’ll no doubt have seen the Night City Trauma Team in action. When someone’s hurt, and can afford the service, they’ll descend from the sky in an armoured vehicle, fend off attackers, and get the victim to safety. Now you get to join them.

The mod’s description says you’ll get an in-game text message asking if you want to join. You then “go to the interview at the Medical Center in Little China, and they put you on probation".

"Then you take the staff elevator to the roof, get changed in the armory, meet your crew and board the AV.”

At the time of writing, there’s only one shift available, but you can repeat it as many times as you want. The AV will transport you to the scene of the crime and once you take down the enemies and retrieve your client you’ll be paid for your troubles.

It’s the kind of side-activity that we’d have loved to see in the full-game as while Night City is gorgeous, there’s very little to do in terms of open-world interactivity.

After taking the Join Trauma Team mod for a spin myself, I can confidently say it’s great, and I’m hoping more missions are added soon.

Weirdly though, it reminded me most of my time with Grand Theft Auto IV … One of my favourite parts of the game was hijacking a police cruiser and using its radio to track down criminals at large, and it was disappointing to see it absent from Grand Theft Auto V .

Given the hype around GTA VI’s open-world, this is the exact type of content I’d love to see return in Leonida, and I think Cyberpunk 2 should consider it too.

Public service vehicles like police cars, ambulances, taxis should all come with unique functionality. It makes the world feel more alive and does wonders for keeping the overall gameplay experience fresh.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Lands on Battle.net at $17.99 Intro Price
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2077 Battle.net launched Nov. 10 with a $17.99 intro price that ends Nov. 16. See prices, the Edgerunners 2 update and what Blizzard says.
items.content:
Image: CD PROJEKT RED Cyberpunk 2077 went on sale in Blizzard’s Battle.net shop on November 10, 2026, and the launch pricing runs out today. According to TalkEsport , the US introductory prices were $17.99 for the base game and $31.99 for the Ultimate Edition, with a stated end date of November 16 and higher prices after that.

What Blizzard and CD PROJEKT RED Launched on November 10 Battle.net Prices: $17.99, $31.99 and the November 16 Deadline What the Edgerunners 2 Update Adds on Battle.net Graphics options and upscaling changes Content, tours and mods How the Battle.net Deal Came Together Why Blizzard Says It Is Not Chasing Steam or Epic Battle.net vs Steam, Epic and GOG: Where the Fourth Storefront Fits Is Battle.net really the fourth store? Market Impact for CD PROJEKT RED: 40 Million Copies and a New Channel Blizzard’s Fall Calendar: WoW Forever, Hearthstone and Now Cyberpunk Launch Problems: Download and Install Reports on Blizzard’s Forums What PC Players Should Do Before the Price Rises The Witcher 3 Pipeline and What Else Could Follow Cyberpunk Historical Context: From a Blizzard-Only Launcher to a Multi-Publisher Shop Five Predictions for Battle.net After Cyberpunk 2077 What Remains Unconfirmed About the Battle.net Launch FAQ: Cyberpunk 2077 on Battle.net Related Coverage Three products arrived together: Cyberpunk 2077, the Phantom Liberty expansion, and Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition, which bundles the two. Every Battle.net version includes the free Edgerunners 2 Update. Coverage calls Battle.net the fourth PC storefront for the game after Steam, GOG and the Epic Games Store, a label that works better as a market description than an official designation.

The launch matters beyond one discount. Battle.net spent years as the home of Blizzard and Activision releases, and a CD PROJEKT RED flagship is its clearest step toward carrying outside publishers. Anyone adding another launcher to a PC also adds another account to protect, which is why a short guide to securing gaming accounts is worth a read before you sign in.

Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.

The release was announced as a partnership between CD PROJEKT RED and Blizzard Entertainment. Blizzard’s own news post, dated November 10, describes the game as out now on Battle.net, and GamerHeadlines reported the same launch the following day. Players can buy the base game, the Phantom Liberty expansion on its own, or the Ultimate Edition that holds both.

One detail trips up shoppers. CD PROJEKT RED’s own pages state that Cyberpunk 2077 is required to play Phantom Liberty, so the expansion is not a standalone purchase in practice. Blizzard’s announcement does not say the expansion comes free with the base game either. If you want both, the Ultimate Edition is the single-click route.

The Battle.net arrival also makes a recent official list out of date. The studio’s Update 2.5 posts from late October named Steam, GOG and the Epic Games Store for PC and Mac, with no mention of Battle.net. That roster no longer matches what a PC shopper sees today.

The game itself is a long-running seller. CD PROJEKT RED has said Cyberpunk 2077 passed 40 million copies sold, and that Phantom Liberty sold 15 million copies in less than three years. A fresh storefront does not change the game, but it does put an established title in front of a different audience at a launch discount.

The reported US launch prices are $17.99 for Cyberpunk 2077 and $31.99 for the Ultimate Edition. Battle.net’s storefront banner advertises savings of up to 70% with an introductory discount. The offer is stated to end on November 16, after which prices will rise. Blizzard’s launch announcement confirms availability but does not publish a price, so the dollar figures come from launch coverage rather than from Blizzard itself.

A little arithmetic shows what the bundle is worth. The Ultimate Edition costs $14 more than the base game at the reported prices, which puts the implied cost of Phantom Liberty inside the bundle at $14. That reading is an inference from two launch prices, not a figure Blizzard published.

For buyers, the practical rule is simple. If the plan is to own both halves of the game on Battle.net, the bundle at $31.99 beats buying pieces. After today, check the live price before assuming any of these numbers still apply, since Blizzard said they will go up.

The Battle.net build ships with Update 2.5, branded the Edgerunners 2 Update. CD PROJEKT RED announced the update alongside the Netflix premiere of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2, and it reached the game’s other platforms on October 22. Battle.net buyers get the same content on day one, with no separate charge.

items.title: GTA VI Owner Takes a Shot at Cyberpunk 2077, Recalls the RPG’s Disastrous Launch, and Believes Delaying Rockstar’s Game Was the Best Decision
items.summary: Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Take-Two Interactive, defended delaying the release of 'Grand Theft Auto VI' to November 2026 to ensure its quality, drawing a comparison to the problematic launch of 'Cyberpunk 2077'. He emphasized the importance of making tough decisions to maintain high standards in game development, contrasting Rockstar's approach with those who rush releases despite potential issues.
items.content:
window.__runDeferredScript({"id":"custom-script-8ccaa8a7","src":"https://t.seedtag.com/t/4204-4423-01.js","strategy":"userInteraction","attributes":{}}); In an alternate reality, Grand Theft Auto VI would have launched late last year. We know that never happened, as the game suffered two delays that pushed its release to November 2026. Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Take-Two Interactive, acknowledges that changing the schedule was a difficult decision, but ultimately believes it was the best thing they could have done.

To make his point, the executive behind Rockstar Games’ parent company brought up a particularly infamous case: Cyberpunk 2077 , which had one of the most disastrous and controversial launches of the decade.

GTA VI was first revealed to the world in December 2023, when its release was confirmed for sometime in fall 2025. Unfortunately, the developers later announced the first delay, pushing its debut to May of the following year.

Just when everything seemed to be going smoothly, Rockstar Games once again took to social media to announce a second change to the release date. Grand Theft Auto VI will now arrive in stores on November 19, and everything seems to indicate that nothing and no one will prevent it from launching on the scheduled date.

In mid-October, studio head Jennifer Kolbe spoke with Bloomberg journalist Jason Schreier and recalled the moment she had to inform Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Take-Two Interactive, about the second delay. “I think he said something like, ‘I can’t believe it! Please tell me you’re joking!’”

In the end, Jennifer Kolbe described the head of Rockstar Games’ parent company as a “very reasonable” person, which is why they were able to secure the extra time needed to finish development.

The topic came up during a recent interview between Strauss Zelnick and the Wall Street Journal . The Take-Two Interactive executive recalled that being told the release date needed to be pushed back was not ideal, but ultimately says he approved the decision to ensure the quality of the product.

“Your mission is to create the best entertainment on Earth, and part of your three-pillar strategy is to be the most creative. And sometimes you have to make those costly and uncomfortable decisions in service of that mission and those goals.”

GTA VI suffered two delays, changing its official release date twice.

While discussing the matter, Strauss Zelnick pointed out that many companies have an excellent vision, a well-defined strategy, and an established culture, but sometimes end up doing things that contradict all of those principles. He explained that moments like these put everyone involved to the test.

The Take-Two Interactive CEO acknowledged that some developers choose to stick to an established release schedule at all costs, leading them to launch games even when they are not ready. Although he did not mention any names, he clearly took a shot at Cyberpunk 2077 .

“I’m not going to blame any competitor, but if you know anything about the videogame industry, you’ll remember that in recent years there was a high-profile launch that fell into this category: they released it, and then had to pull it from the market after launch because it didn’t work,” Strauss Zelnick commented.

Of course, several other games have also had to be removed from digital storefronts after launching with serious problems. One of the most recent examples is SEGA’s Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition . However, to be fair, CD Projekt RED’s RPG is one of the few cases that fit the category of “high-profile launches.”

Cyberpunk 2077 debuted in 2020, but all of its versions suffered from technical issues, bugs, and other errors that hurt the experience. As a result, the game was removed from Sony’s PlayStation Store, and the developers offered refunds. The controversy also led to a class-action lawsuit against CD Projekt RED.

items.title: From the Anime to the Game — Free Update Brings Edgerunners 2 Content and More to Cyberpunk 2077!
items.summary: The free Edgerunners 2 Update to Cyberpunk 2077 is available now, with content inspired by the second installment of the hit anime series now streaming on Netflix
items.content:
“Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2” premiered on Netflix on October 20, bringing a whole new cast of characters to Night City for a dark, gritty ride. And now we’re bringing a little piece of that story into Cyberpunk 2077 , too! The free Edgerunners 2 Update is here, with content inspired by the anime, new ways to fight, more customization options, and plenty of other additions.

We’ve got a lot to cover, so let’s get into it. And don’t worry if you haven’t watched the new anime yet — no “Edgerunners 2” spoilers ahead!

One of the things we love about Night City is that there’s always another story unfolding somewhere. V may be central to the events of Cyberpunk 2077 , but they’re hardly the only merc in town, fighting to survive and make a name for themselves on those neon-soaked streets. Every fixer has clients, every crew has gigs to take care of, every Night City merc has their story — and sometimes, those stories collide in unexpected ways.

That’s exactly what happens in the brand-new quest introduced with the “Edgerunners 2” Update. What begins as just another gig from Wakako turns into an action-packed, high-stakes mission that sees V cross paths with Weak Kingsley, a famed Night City merc and one of the main characters of “Edgerunners 2.” We won’t spoil what happens, but during the course of this mission, V has a chance to assist Weak and his crew during a risky gig that takes place in a brand-new location: Night City Prison.

The new “Edgerunners 2” gig is more than a chance to encounter characters from the anime in the game — it serves as a prequel to the events of the series. So, play the quest before watching the anime, and you’ll have a little extra context going into Episode 1. Already seen the show? Then with this gig, you’ll get to revisit part of Weak’s story with a broader perspective of him and his crew.

And there’s even more forEdgerunnersfans in this update. For starters, you can find and equip Weak’s full outfit — vest, glasses, coat, pants, the works — and get your hands on his signature revolver, Coronation. We’ve also added a new radio station, HKGN 102.FM, featuring official tracks from both “Cyberpunk: Edgerunners” and “Edgerunners 2.” So if you’re planning to spend a few more hours cruising around Night City after watching the show, we’ve got your soundtrack covered.

What’s better than blasting your way through a warehouse full of gangoons with a revolver, dealing one headshot after another? Doing it with two revolvers, obviously.

That’s right — dual wielding is here! With the Edgerunners 2 Update, you can raise hell with a pistol or revolver in each hand. That’s a whole new vibe — and a whole new level of awesome.

But dual wielding isn’t just about looking cool. It brings a new playstyle and a fresh way to approach combat — in fact, it’s one of the most significant gameplay additions to the game’s combat since Update 2.0 introduced throwing knives. So if you’ve been looking for an excuse to shake up your fighting style, this might just be it.

Cyberware enhances your stats and abilities — but what if it could take your style to the next level, too? That’s where glamdocs come in. These new vendors let you customize the appearance of your cyberware, with 40 styles in different colors to choose from. Fancy a new look for your chrome? Pay them a visit at one (or all) of the five locations across Night City and see what catches your eye.

In a city that lives and dies by appearances, V really can’t afford to pass up any opportunity to shake up their look. On top of cyberware customization, we’ve also added 20 new hairstyles and several clothing sets to give your V the best chance of standing out, even in Night City.

We know how creative the Cyberpunk 2077 community can be, and we’re always curious to see what players come up with. That’s why we’re introducing cross-platform mod support through mod.io integration.

The update adds a Mods panel where you can browse and install supported community-created content directly in the game. It’s a new way to experiment with your experience, and we’re looking forward to seeing how it develops as more mods become available and receive support over time!

We’ve covered some of the bigger additions, but there’s still plenty to find in the Edgerunners 2 Update.

items.content:
Thought you were done with Night City? Well, Night City's not quite done with you!

Patch notes for Cyberpunk 2077's Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) are now available for your early perusal before the update hits the streets on October 22nd. Watch the Features Overview video to see some of the new features in action:

And if you want to know even more, read through the list of most important changes below:

Edgerunners Content

  • Added a new side quest, Clampdown, set before the events of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2. To unlock it, complete The Heist and two gigs for Wakako, then wait for a message from her.

    [/*]

  • Added a new 5-piece gear set based on the character King, which can be obtained during the Clampdown side quest.

    [/*]

  • Added a new radio station, HKGN 102.0 FM, featuring a selection of tracks from the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners series.

    [/*]

Show Off

  • A brand-new clothing collection has arrived in Night City! 5 new outfit sets can now be purchased from certain clothing vendors:

    • Maxiwear: available in Heywood, Arroyo, Little China

      [/*]

    • Jinguji: available in City Center

      [/*]

    • NetWatch: available in Kabuki, Japantown

      [/*]

    • IconAmerica: available in Pacifica, Badlands, Northside

      [/*]

    • And one more set that will hit Night City shelves just a little later...

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • The NUS Infiltrator clothing set can be now purchased from clothing vendors in Kabuki and Japantown.

    [/*]

  • 4 new TWINTONE skins for Quadra Turbo-R V-Tech are now available via Twitch Drops.

    [/*]

  • Some of the hairstyles that were previously exclusive to NPCs are now available for V. Please note that some hairstyles are available only to feminine or masculine body types.

    [/*]

  • Show off your chrome! You can now customize your hand cyberware. Equip your Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire or Projectile Launch System, and visit one of 5 Glamdocs (marked with a spray paint icon on the map) to give your implants a fresh, new look. Each Glamdoc is located in a unique shop, along with their own intro scene with voiceover and animations, and offers a unique catalog of cyberware skins with customizable colors.

    [/*]

  • Sometimes one gun just isn't enough. The new Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree (along with four auxiliary perks) introduces an entirely new playstyle, allowing you to dual-wield Pistols and Revolvers from the Power category.

    [/*]

  • Added frames from the Cyberpunk Trading Card Game to Photo Mode, allowing you to make your preem shots look like custom cards.

    [/*]

  • Added new poses in Photo Mode to show off your dual-wielding prowess.

    [/*]

Mod the World

Added Cross-Platform Mod Support, powered by mod.io, a first step into cross-platform modding that allows you to easily browse and install a selection of player-created mods directly from the in-game menu. More mods will become available over time. The feature is available on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S.

Upgrading the World

  • Welcome to Paradise! Added a new side quest that takes you on a journey to uncover a mystery and explore Night City on a guided tour narrated by Richard Night. It unlocks after completing The Heist and reaching level 15 Street Cred.

    [/*]

  • Added 12 new Minor Arcana Tarot Cards to discover across Night City. The Tarot menu now has separate sections for Major and Minor Arcana. The new tarot cards are part of a new side quest, an extension of Fool on the Hill, which activates after scanning any of the new cards. Collect them all to get a special reward.

    [/*]

Quality of Life

  • Saves in the “Load Game” menu are now grouped by separate playthroughs.

    [/*]

  • Added item filters to apartment and vehicle stashes.

    [/*]

  • Modded saves in the "Load Game" menu are now marked with a dedicated icon. Please note that achievements and trophies cannot be earned while playing on console from a modded save file.

    [/*]

  • Updated the selection of AMD FSR options. FSR 3 upscaling is no longer included, while FSR 2.1, FSR 4, and FSR 3.1 Frame Generation remain available.

    [/*]

  • Updated the CD PROJEKT RED Account connection, My Rewards and telemetry consent menus.

    [/*]

Technology

  • Added support for DLSS 4.5, including up to 6X Multi Frame Generation or Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and the 2nd Generation Transformer Model.

    [/*]

  • Added support for glasses-free 3D effects on compatible Samsung Odyssey 3D monitors, along with a Motion Comfort setting that lets you balance 3D depth and viewing comfort.

    [/*]

  • Added support for MetalFX Frame Interpolation on Mac.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle in settings for FSR Anti-Lag 2.

    [/*]

  • Introduced various performance optimizations, including improvements specifically for Ray Tracing.

    [/*]

  • Improved HDR rendering to provide more accurate colors, brightness, and contrast on compatible displays.

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Things Done Changed- Fixed an issue where the Delamain cab could get stuck after crashing into another vehicle, blocking quest progression.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where enabling Film Grain had no effect.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where tagging enemies while scanning could also cause V to crouch or stand up when using certain control schemes.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where controller settings for the Third-Person Camera were missing.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several typos in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added various other fixes for features and content introduced since Patch 2.1.

    [/*]

items.content:
To survive in Night City, you need someone to watch your back. On the way to the major leagues, V managed to gather a remarkable crew. You could even say, a crew to remember!

From trusted allies to unforgettable personalities, these are the people who helped shape V’s journey through the City of Dreams. This episode of It’s All About You is dedicated to the legendary crew that stood by V through every high and low.

Thank you for staying with us and expressing your love for Cyberpunk 2077 in the most creative ways possible. Don’t forget to check out our gallery to see more works, and, of course, share your creations with us: http://cdpred.ly/AAY

See you in the next episode!

items.content:
Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥

Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey!

Sure, the city’s full of noise — sirens, synths, gunfire in the distance — but if there’s one song that became its soul, it’s “Never Fade Away.”

We brought together legendary artists from across the city of dreams to reinterpret this iconic track — each in their own voice, their own style, their own rebellion. ❤️‍🔥

Plug in, turn it up, and dive into our latest It’s All About You episode.

Because legends don’t fade.
